solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game of cards a Celt played

indicators.note: played suggests the cards are dealt and shuffled about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card game in which a Celtic player takes part.
explanation.definitionFit: This string figure pastime, passed hand to hand between two players, is a traditional children's game.

clue.text: Nicks and Jeans?

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for to steal, and so is to trouser money
jeans are one kind of legwear covering each leg separately; the question mark flags definition by example

explanation.surface: Two names, Nick and Jean, apparently paired up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, the word means pockets or steals, a British slang sense; read as a noun it is the garments of which jeans are an example. Capitals disguise both as people's names.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocketing something dishonestly is slang for stealing, matching nicks; and jeans are an example of legwear.

clue.text: A large gamble taking on queen and her mate?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: taking on means the gamble word takes the queen's letter into itself

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: Someone making a big bet on a queen and her consort.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen does double duty: R inside BET, and the queen whose mate is meant, Victoria, whose husband was Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was the husband and consort of Queen Victoria, so he was the queen's mate.

clue.text: Hot working up around Kent? Never!

parts.note: hot means fashionable, which is in

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for working is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
CA, short for circa, means around or approximately
Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: An indignant refusal of hot work being done around Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ON to NO; CA is circa; Kent is the English county in the South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means under no circumstances whatever, an emphatic way of saying never.

clue.text: Swimmer embarrassed daughter around company

indicators.note: around means the letters for embarrassed daughter sit on either side of the company letters

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A swimmer's daughter turns red in front of company.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish, a species of rockfish, and in crosswords any fish can be called a swimmer.

clue.text: Get on with male revolutionary — super!

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A cheer for getting on with a male rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for great or excellent, an exclamation of enthusiastic approval like super.

clue.text: Dry white? Just lovely to look at!

definitions.meaning: dry weather without rain is described as fine and pleasant
pale or light-coloured skin or hair is described with this word
beautiful, an old-fashioned sense as in 'my ... lady'

explanation.surface: A wine buff describing a dry white wine as lovely to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: A quadruple definition: four senses of the one word, disguised as a wine description.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers dry weather, a pale complexion, equitable treatment and beauty, each a separate dictionary sense.

clue.text: Foreign city son alleges corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son claims that some city overseas is corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian city is a foreign one from the British newspaper's point of view.

clue.text: Miles not bored around music producer

indicators.note: around means moved about, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Miles Davis, never bored, hanging around a music producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' suggests the jazz trumpeter, which fits the brass instrument nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument with a sliding tube produces music, so it is cryptically a music producer.

clue.text: Take on a small European without problem

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the other letters go around the problem word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Taking on a small European who is free of problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, so A S E wraps around SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or responsibility is to assume it, as in assuming command.

clue.text: Press conservative boy that's inflexible

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A newspaper, a Tory and a young man who won't bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally armour-plated, the word now means rigid and unbreakable, as in a cast-iron guarantee.

clue.text: A rare break with drugs for one in custody?

parts.note: R is a less common abbreviation for rare
a rest is a break
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so two of them are drugs

explanation.surface: A rare holiday break with drugs on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: R for rare is an unusual abbreviation found in some dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taken in by the police is held in custody, as a detained person.

clue.text: Runs away from first of lancehead vipers

indicators.note: away from means the chosen letter is removed from the word for runs

parts.note: runs in stockings or tights are ladders in British English

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the snake name lancehead

explanation.surface: Fleeing from the lead lancehead snake among vipers.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in tights; a lancehead is itself a viper, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the only venomous snakes native to Britain, members of the viper family.

clue.text: Secret dirt could be made thus

definitions.text: Secret dirt could be made thus

indicators.note: could be made signals that the letters can be remade into another word

explanation.surface: Classified scandal could be turned into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes how secret dirt might be classified: kept confidential and not for public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret information is given limited circulation, cleared for only a few, as classified material.

clue.text: Annoyed? So issue direct rude remarks!

indicators.note: annoyed means stirred up or disturbed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An irritated person told to go and make rude comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite comments are acts of bad manners, the plural of incivility.

clue.text: Occasionally switch positions

definitions.meaning: the two settings of a light switch

explanation.surface: Sometimes swapping places.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intermittently, and it also names the two settings a switch may be in.

clue.text: Popular record I have still?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
an act is a formal record, as of Parliament
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claiming they still have a popular record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless and not moving or working is still; the question mark notes the stretch.

clue.text: Complaint about light infantry's doctrine?

indicators.note: about means the complaint word surrounds the infantry letters

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
LI is the abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: A grumble about the doctrine of the light infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed or tenet that someone holds true is a conviction; the question mark marks it as loose.

clue.text: Prisoner beaten at chess?

definitions.meaning: a person held in a jail
read as '...', checkmated and so beaten at chess

explanation.surface: A jailbird who lost a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words: a king in mate has lost the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held in a prison is a fellow detainee; split, the word means checkmated.

clue.text: Service a church holds finally for butcher

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: holds means the church letters contain the chosen letter

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word for

explanation.surface: A church service held up at last on account of a butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of 'for', which sits inside A CE to give ACRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to slaughter them in large numbers, a verb sense matching this word.

clue.text: Celebrities welcoming one in Steps

indicators.note: welcoming means the celebrities word takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: stars are celebrities
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Celebrities welcoming a member into the pop group Steps.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps, capitalised, looks like the British pop group, but it is the flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps leading between floors is a staircase.

clue.text: Order given to old Royal Marine

parts.note: a command is an order

explanation.surface: An order given to a retired Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's Royal Marines are an amphibious force whose members earn the green beret of a special assault soldier.

clue.text: Work over drink? That'll need reviewing!

indicators.note: reviewing hints at looking back, so the letters are read in reverse in this down clue

parts.note: to sup is to drink
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Work done over a drink will need checking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a work is used for a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: American jerks pinching knight for larks

indicators.note: pinching means the other letters grip the knight letter inside them

parts.note: tics are involuntary jerks
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: American idiots stealing a knight's piece for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are pranks and high jinks, playful mischievous behaviour.

clue.text: One selling lots of our nice tea at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seller of large quantities of our fine tea on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' seems to mean plenty, but they are the items for sale at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running an auction sells items in lots, numbered batches put up for bids.

clue.text: Struggle with expectation

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Struggling with what one expects.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something in prospect, as in 'with a view to', means having it as an expectation or intention.
